name: fig31_replica_vs_direct_entropy
caption: Replica identity for a random d = 8 density matrix (S_vN = 1.503146). (a) ln Tr rho^n and its tangent at n = 1. (b) Finite-difference error: quadratic in h for the central difference and quartic for Richardson down to a round-off floor of ~1e-10..1e-11. (c) In finite dimension the continuation from integer replicas alone (polynomial interpolation) converges only slowly; gravitational path integrals provide only integer-n data, which is why the analytic continuation is the hard step there. A finite-dimensional calculation is not a gravitational path integral.
